entities.name: Meleager of Gadara
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Meleager of Gadara, flourishing around 140–70 BCE, stands as a pivotal figure in Hellenistic Greek literature, primarily celebrated as a master epigrammatist and the compiler of the earliest known anthology of Greek poetry, his *Garland* (Στέφανος). Hailing from Gadara, a vibrant Hellenistic city in Coele-Syria, he bridged the literary traditions of the Greek mainland with the cosmopolitan intellectual centers of the Eastern Mediterranean, significantly shaping the transmission and appreciation of the Greek epigram. His work provides invaluable insight into the aesthetic sensibilities and literary trends of the late Hellenistic period, combining erudition with a distinctly personal and often sensual voice.

Meleager’s monumental achievement, the *Garland*, was a collection of epigrams by some 46 earlier and contemporary poets, from Archilochus to himself, arranged alphabetically by the initial letter of each poet's name. This innovative structure, described as 'the first systematic anthology of Greek verse,' preserved a vast body of work that might otherwise have been lost, including fragments of Sappho, Alcaeus, and Anacreon, alongside numerous Hellenistic poets. Beyond his role as an editor, Meleager was a prolific poet in his own right, with 134 of his own epigrams surviving. These range from deeply personal expressions of love, desire, and loss, often addressed to specific individuals like Heliodora or Zenophila, to satirical pieces, riddles, and dedicatory verses, showcasing a remarkable breadth of thematic and stylistic mastery.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Meleager's *Garland* was the foundational anthology of Greek epigrams, preserving countless works and directly influencing the later *Palatine Anthology*, thus shaping the transmission of Hellenistic poetry to the modern era.
